articles.title: Seth Rogen Tells TIFF the Best Advice He’s Ever Received: ‘Less Semen, More Emotion!’
articles.summary: It’s extraordinary just how prolific Seth Rogen has been. He began performing stand-up comedy at clubs around his native Vancouver at the age of 13 — around the time he and his buddy Evan Goldberg would write the first draft of “Superbad” — before featuring in the Judd Apatow shows “Freaks and…
body: Prior to the ceremony, Rogen sat down for a career-spanning talk with Geoff Macnaughton, TIFF’s vice president of market programming at theatrical, at the fest’s John Bassett Theatre. The multi-hyphenate has two films at this year’s fest — “Babies,” an ensemble comedy directed by his wife Lauren Miller Rogen, and “Tangles,” an animated film which the Rogens produced. And it was quite the hot ticket (though that’s to be expected for the hometown hero).
The talk began with Macnaughton asking about Rogen’s beginning as a teenage stand-up in clubs around Vancouver.

“My first show was at a lesbian bar called The Lotus. It went very well,” he laughed. “I don’t know. I think I’m very lucky that from a very young age, I kind of knew what I wanted to do. As soon as I realized you could be funny for a living, and I loved films … and I wanted to make movies. I got a video camera and made movies with my dear friend Evan, who I still make movies with today. I was just very fortunate in that I had a very clear idea of what I wanted to do with my life, and my parents were very supportive of it.”

articles.title: Teary-Eyed Kaley Cuoco Recalls Death of Her ‘8 Simple Rules’ TV Dad John Ritter: ‘One of the Worst Days of My Life’
articles.summary: Kaley Cuoco stepped out Saturday night to pay tribute to her TV dad, John Ritter. She was starring as the television sitcom icon’s daughter on “8 Simple Rules” in 2003 when Ritter suffered a fatal thoracic aortic dissection – a tearing of the heart’s main artery — while on set. “I always cry when I
body: When the Emmy-winning Ritter walked over to her at the table, Cuoco introduced herself. “He gives me a big hug, and he looks at me, and he takes off his jacket, and he puts it on me and says, ‘Don’t ever wear that again,’” Cuoco said, smiling. “It was the best.”
Ritter appeared in the first season of “8 Simple Rules” and three episodes of the second before his untimely passing at age 54.
“He was so funny,” she said. “I took all that with me in life and the jobs I had after. He always has been the north star in my career and somebody who I adore.”

The gala was hosted by Ritter’s widow, Amy Yasbeck, and his son, Tyler Ritter. Yasbeck reunited with her co-stars from the sitcom “Wings” – Tim Daly, Steve Webber and Tony Shalhoub – for a Q&A moderated by Variety’ s Marc Malkin. Writer and producer Steve Levitan also joined the panel and recalled how “Wings” was his first writing job in Hollywood.

articles.title: Hollywood Ventures Group, Canada’s Big Picture Cinema Group, and Morocco’s Pink Sheep Team on Casablanca-Set Thriller ‘The Final Bet’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Hollywood Ventures Group (HVG), Canadian film finance and production outfit Big Picture Cinema Group, and Morocco’s Pink Sheep Productions are teaming up to bring bestselling Moroccan crime thriller “The Final Bet” to the big screen.
body: “It is a great source of pride to see ‘The Final Bet’ move from the page to the screen,” Hamdouchi said in a statement.

“A novel lives through language and imagination, and cinema gives its characters, tensions and story an entirely new dimension through image, performance and sound,” the Moroccan author added. “To see this Moroccan story take on a new life as a feature film is deeply meaningful to me, both personally and as a writer,” he added.

Hollywood Ventures Group co-founder Glenn Gainor commented: “While this is a work of fiction, it speaks to a period of profound legal and social change in Morocco and to questions of justice that transcend borders. We’re incredibly proud to help bring Abdelilah Hamdouchi’s story to the screen.”
The producers are shopping the project at the Toronto film market and targeting a 2027 start of production date.

articles.title: 'Nepo baby is a horrific term,' says Zeta-Jones
articles.summary: The Chicago star's children Dylan and Carys have both gone into showbiz, following in her footsteps.
body: Hollywood star Catherine Zeta-Jones has declared the phrase "nepo baby" is "horrific", saying: "These kids didn't ask to be born into this."
The term refers to children of famous parents perceived to have achieved riches and success off their parents' backs.
The 56-year-old actress, married to Kirk Douglas' son Michael Douglas, has two children - Dylan and Carys - who have both followed their parents into showbiz.
Dylan, she said, was pursuing acting while Carys was interested in directing. She told The Sunday Times they were "plugging away".

articles.title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom review – Aardman’s spooky-season caper sparkles with fun
articles.summary: There’s trouble afoot when Shaun’s pumpkin-supersizing serum ends up in a balding farmer’s hair growth bottle in this third cinematic adventure. Summer is over and Halloween is on the way … not for a fair bit, of course, but if all the UK’s Halloween merch and continuing pop culture content is up…
body: The pitchfork-wielding villagers of Mossy Bottom are hilariously stunned at the terrifying appearance of a rampaging, hairy beast who has been spotted in the outlying fields and woodlands at the very moment that the farmer himself has mysteriously disappeared. Has the beast somehow kidnapped or eaten the farmer? It is a nightmarish mystery that will need every ounce of Shaun and his pals’ courage and ingenuity to sort out, not to mention that of the vet, who uses a hi-tech DNA machine to examine the genetic provenance of a piece of the beast’s fur she has managed to snip off.

It is a love story of sorts, perhaps a little like that of Beauty and the Beast, but about two people who for most the story’s running time don’t know that they are going to be in love. As for the sheep, their faces convey amazingly distinct expressions and moods with just a few deft movements. It’s sharp, smart, funny and precise; there is nothing woolly about it.
points: There’s trouble afoot when Shaun’s pumpkin-supersizing serum ends up in a balding farmer’s hair growth bottle in this third cinematic adventure.

articles.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother review – Mahershala Ali is a grieving hitman in soulful thriller
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: the two-time Oscar-winner is an unusual killer in a compelling mix of pulpy action and family drama. Latif, the solemn hitman played soulfully by Mahershala Ali, carries diapers in his kill kit.
body: Those contradictions are on full striking display in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’s opening moments, an explosive close-quarters brawl in a restroom, after which Latif uses the baby wipes to clean up the mess he made with that blade. It’s a lovely image, in a film filled with so many, cutting right through the tension within this character. It also feels like a wink to the audience from Ali and writer/director Bassam Tariq, a way for them to acknowledge right off the top the distracting mess made by that other Blade.

Tariq and Ali were collaborating on Marvel’s Blade reboot. Ali was announced to star as the vampire-slayer formerly played by Wesley Snipes all the way back in 2019. Tariq signed on to write and direct in 2021 but departed a year later. Ali recently revealed that, after being strung along for seven years in development, the reboot was not happening. It’s easy to assume that some of the ideas Tariq and Ali had for Blade made their way into this new collaboration, in which Ali gets to finally wield a blade and John Cho, of Harold and Kumar fame, stuns as a vampiric foe. The echoes and parallels are there but minimal, perhaps even coincidental.

articles.title: ‘Babies’ Review: Anna Kendrick Is a Comic Dynamo Alongside Seth Rogen in a Sparkling Portrait of a Couple Weighing the Pros and Cons of Parenthood
articles.summary: A longtime couple reconsiders their choice to remain childless in this film written and directed by Rogen's real-life wife, Lauren Miller Rogen.
body: To be or not to be … parents. That is the thorny question raised in Lauren Miller Rogen’s Babies, an astute charmer about a happy, supportive Los Angeles couple ( Anna Kendrick and Seth Rogen ) who, after 17 years of togetherness, begin wondering if they might be missing a bouncing bundle of something in their lives.

Drawing from aspects of her own life, Miller, in her second directorial effort following 2018’s Like Father, taps into a reservoir of considerable relevance here, finding plenty of fertile comic ground in the subject matter but never at the expense of weightier questions surrounding life choices, human existence and the uncertain state of society.

With an especially terrific Kendrick serving as Miller’s onscreen surrogate, Babies should have no problem finding an adoring audience when it lands in theaters via Roadside Attractions and Vertical sometime next year.
points: A longtime couple reconsiders their choice to remain childless in this film written and directed by Rogen's real-life wife, Lauren Miller Rogen.
